newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CPC delays leaded reformate award, buys unleaded.
newsitem.headline: CPC delays leaded reformate award, buys unleaded.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) will award its leaded 95-octane reformate tender on April 3, but has bought unleaded reformate for first-half May delivery at $27.40 a barrel cost-and-freight, a CPC official said on Wednesday.
"We will award the leaded only tomorrow because the price is not so good," the official said.
The leaded cargo was offered at $28.40 per barrel, c-and-f basis.
The tender, which closed on April 1 and valid for two days, required the two 250,000-barrel leaded and unleaded reformate cargoes to be delivered to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohsiung or Shalung.

The unleaded cargo, was said to have been sold by a South Korean refiner at a surprisingly low level, since 95-octane unleaded cargoes was bid on Wednesday at $27.50 free-on-board (fob) Singapore for April 17-21 lifting, traders said.
The Singapore market was on the long side with prices in Singapore crashing by more than $1.00 per barrel on Monday to trade at $27.00, fob basis.
"We received so many offers..14 when normally its around 10," a CPC source said.
In its last tender, CPC bought 250,000 barrels of unleaded reformate at a much higher price of $28.60 per barrel, c-and-f basis for April 16-30 arrival.
Leaded reformate was last awarded at $29.00 per barrel for first half April delivery, c-and-f basis.
